title: Section 8.0 Creating and Using Workflow Actions

source.author: Written for this study guide
source.grounding: help.splunk.com Splunk Enterprise 10.4, Knowledge Management Manual and workflow_actions.conf spec

questions.stem: How many values does the Action type setting of a workflow action have, and what are they?

options.text: Two: link and search
options.explanation: GET and POST are both link actions, separated by the Link method setting. In workflow_actions.conf the setting is `type` with values link or search.

options.text: Three: GET, POST and Search
options.explanation: This mirrors the blueprint wording of objective 8.1 and is exactly why it is a good distractor. GET and POST are not action types.

options.text: Four: GET, POST, Search and Link
options.explanation: Adding Link to the three does not fix the underlying error.

options.text: Two: GET and POST
options.explanation: This drops the search action entirely, which is one of the two real types.

questions.overallExplanation: The blueprint names three kinds of workflow action, but the configuration has two types. A GET and a POST are both `type = link`, distinguished by `link.method = get` or `post`.

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe the function of GET, POST, and Search workflow actions
guide.verdictNote: Reading the blueprint wording as a configuration list is the mistake. Objective titles describe capabilities, not settings.

docs.title: workflow_actions.conf spec (Admin Manual 10.4)
docs.note: type is link or search; link.method selects get or post.

questions.stem: A workflow action stanza sets `type = link` and `link.uri` but omits `link.method`. What happens?

options.text: A GET is issued, because link.method defaults to get.
options.explanation: The default makes the stanza valid and functional. Only type and label are required, plus link.uri for a link action.

options.text: Nothing happens; the action is inert without a method.
options.explanation: The default supplies the method, so the action works.

options.text: The stanza is invalid and is ignored at load time.
options.explanation: It is a complete and valid link action.

options.text: A POST is issued, because POST is the safer default.
options.explanation: There is no safety-based default. GET is the documented one.

questions.overallExplanation: Required settings are type and label, plus link.uri for a link action or search.search_string for a search action. Everything else has a default, and link.method defaults to get.

guide.verdictNote: link.target defaults to blank, meaning a new window, and search.target works the same way.

docs.title: workflow_actions.conf spec (Admin Manual 10.4)
docs.note: link.method default is get; link.target default is blank.

questions.stem: The "Apply only to the following fields" box is left empty. Where does the workflow action appear?

options.text: Everywhere, because `fields` defaults to `*`.
options.explanation: The wildcard matches all fields, so an unrestricted action is offered on every event and field menu it is eligible for.

options.text: Nowhere, because no field has been nominated.
options.explanation: An empty restriction is not an empty allowlist. Restriction is opt-in.

options.text: Only on the event menu, never on field menus.
options.explanation: That would be a display_location question, and its default is both.

options.text: Only on fields that are in Selected Fields.
options.explanation: The sidebar's selection has no bearing on workflow action scope.

questions.overallExplanation: Two independent defaults make a new action broadly visible: `fields` defaults to `*` and `display_location` defaults to `both`, so it appears in the event menu and in every field menu.

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe the function of GET, POST, and Search workflow actions
guide.verdictNote: Scope is controlled by fields and eventtypes only. There is no sourcetype setting on the form or in the conf file.

docs.title: Control workflow action appearance (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: fields defaults to * and display_location defaults to both.

questions.stem: A workflow action sets `fields = src_ip, dest_ip`. When is it offered?

options.text: Only when both fields are present on the event.
options.explanation: The field list is a conjunction. Every field named must be present before the action applies.

options.text: When either field is present.
options.explanation: Reading the list as a disjunction is the common error. It is an AND, not an OR.

options.text: When at least one field is present and the event has an event type.
options.explanation: Event types are a separate, independent restriction under the eventtypes setting.

options.text: Always, because listing fields only affects the menu label.
options.explanation: The field list genuinely restricts where the action appears.

questions.overallExplanation: All listed fields must be present. The documented example `*, ip_client, ip_server` is explicit about this, which is also why including the wildcard alongside named fields does not loosen the requirement.

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe the function of GET, POST, and Search workflow actions
guide.verdictNote: The `$@field_name$` and `$@field_value$` tokens only resolve from a field menu, so a generic per-field action has to be scoped with fields rather than left global.

docs.title: Control workflow action appearance (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: All fields in the list must be present for the action to apply.

questions.stem: How are POST arguments transmitted, compared with GET?

options.text: HTTP-form encoded in the request body, so they do not appear in the URL or browser history.
options.explanation: POST arguments are configured as link.postargs key and value pairs and are sent in the body rather than the query string.

options.text: Appended to the URI as query parameters, exactly like GET.
options.explanation: That would make POST a GET with extra configuration, which is precisely the misconception.

options.text: Encrypted, which is why POST is preferred for sensitive values.
options.explanation: Nothing about POST encrypts anything. Transport security depends entirely on whether the URI is https.

options.text: As HTTP headers rather than as a body or a query string.
options.explanation: Headers are not where the postargs settings put values.

questions.overallExplanation: POST guarantees placement, not confidentiality. Keeping a value out of the URL and out of browser history is a real benefit, but only https protects it in transit.

guide.verdictNote: Encoding also differs by destination: values in link.uri are URI encoded automatically, POST argument values are HTTP-form encoded automatically.

docs.title: Set up a POST workflow action (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: POST arguments are sent as form-encoded key-value pairs.

questions.stem: A search workflow action sets `search.earliest = -7d` and `search.preserve_timerange = true`. What time range does the secondary search use?

options.text: The last seven days; preserve_timerange is ignored when earliest or latest is set.
options.explanation: An explicit bound wins, and the preserve setting has no effect at all in that case.

options.text: The originating search's range, because preserve_timerange takes precedence.
options.explanation: That would be true only if neither earliest nor latest were set.

options.text: The intersection of the two, so the narrower range applies.
options.explanation: No intersection is computed. One setting simply overrides the other.

options.text: All time, because the conflicting settings cancel out.
options.explanation: Nothing cancels. The explicit bound is used.

questions.overallExplanation: To inherit the originating search's range, set preserve_timerange and leave both bounds unset. Setting either bound silently disables the preserve behaviour.

guide.verdictNote: Two more search-action defaults: search.app defaults to the current app and search.view to the current view, so the secondary search opens wherever the analyst already was.

docs.title: Set up a search workflow action (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: preserve_timerange is ignored if earliest or latest is specified.

questions.stem: Which setting supplies the text a searcher sees in the workflow action menu?

options.text: Label, which also accepts `$field$` tokens
options.explanation: Label is the menu text and is the field that supports token substitution, so a menu entry can include a value from the event.

options.text: Name, which becomes the stanza header
options.explanation: Name is the internal identifier and becomes the stanza header in workflow_actions.conf. It is not what the searcher reads.

options.text: Both, since Name is shown when Label is empty
options.explanation: There is no documented fallback of that kind. Label is a required setting.

options.text: link.uri, whose hostname is displayed
options.explanation: The target URI is never used as the menu text.

questions.overallExplanation: Name is internal, Label is what people see, and Label is where tokens work. A label can be static or include field values, so tokens are supported and never required.

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe the function of GET, POST, and Search workflow actions
guide.verdictNote: No Splunk documentation forbids spaces in a workflow action name. The shipped workflow_actions.conf.example defines stanzas whose names contain spaces.

docs.title: About workflow actions in Splunk Web (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: Label is the menu text and supports field tokens; Name is the internal identifier.

questions.stem: What does a workflow action do to the events it appears on?

options.text: Nothing. It creates no field and modifies no event; it fires only when a person clicks it.
options.explanation: A workflow action is an interactive shortcut in Splunk Web. It has no effect on the data or the result set.

options.text: It adds a field holding the target URI.
options.explanation: No field is created by a workflow action.

options.text: It triggers automatically whenever a matching event is returned.
options.explanation: Automatic responses to conditions are alert actions on a saved search, not workflow actions.

options.text: It enriches the event with data retrieved from the target system.
options.explanation: Nothing is retrieved back into the search. The action opens a link or launches a second search.

questions.overallExplanation: Workflow actions are click-driven navigation, not data processing. If a question describes something happening automatically or a field appearing, the answer is an alert action or a lookup rather than a workflow action.

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe the function of GET, POST, and Search workflow actions
guide.verdictNote: This is the conceptual question in 8.0 most likely to appear, because the other three sub-objectives are configuration detail.

docs.title: About workflow actions in Splunk Web (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: Workflow actions create interactive links and searches from events and fields.

questions.stem: Which two settings restrict where a workflow action appears? (Choose two.)

options.text: `fields`
options.explanation: Lists the fields that must all be present on the event. Defaults to the wildcard.

options.text: `eventtypes`
options.explanation: Limits the action to events carrying the named event types, and is independent of the field restriction.

options.text: `sourcetype`
options.explanation: There is no sourcetype setting in workflow_actions.conf and none on the form. Listing sourcetype under fields does not achieve it either.

options.text: `index`
options.explanation: Index is not a scope for workflow actions any more than it is for props.conf settings.

questions.overallExplanation: Scope is fields and eventtypes only, and display_location decides which menus it can appear in. Any answer naming a source type or an index as a workflow action scope is wrong on the configuration alone.

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe the function of GET, POST, and Search workflow actions
guide.verdictNote: Because eventtypes is a scope, tagging and event types feed directly into workflow action targeting, which is one of the few real cross-links between sections 6.0 and 8.0.

docs.title: workflow_actions.conf spec (Admin Manual 10.4)
docs.note: fields and eventtypes are the scoping settings; no sourcetype setting exists.
